gold.question: Regarding GV-1-2 on the P&ID: It's letting fluid through when it should be shut. What usually causes that and how do I fix it?

candidate: GV-1-2 is a globe valve in the discharge line from pump P-1-1, upstream of ball valve PV-1-1. A globe valve passing fluid when it should be shut is usually caused by seat or disc damage — wear, erosion, or debris (e.g., a particle or weld slug) lodged on the sealing face — or a stem/disc connection failure that prevents the disc from seating. Fix it by closing upstream and downstream isolation (note PV-1-1 downstream) and depressurizing/draining the line, then inspect: lap or re-seat the disc and seat ring or replace the trim, replace the gasket if the leak is at the bonnet or flanges, and verify the disc is properly attached to the stem and the valve is fully turned to the closed position before returning to service.
